title: Stale feed and transport silence
content: Compare tick age and receipt heartbeat. A websocket disconnect, DNS failure, or network path interruption can stop fresh quotes. Inspect transport logs and connection metrics before a simulated reconnect.

title: Exchange rate limits and retry storms
content: HTTP 429 with Retry-After indicates exchange throttling. Check retry pacing and rejected requests. Use bounded backoff; do not replay orders blindly.

title: Slow SQL query and order backlog
content: High SQL duration alongside fill latency suggests a slow query or database contention. Inspect query duration and connection saturation. A busy CPU or bad routing deployment needs different evidence.

title: Retained buffers and memory pressure
content: Growing retained buffer bytes alongside fill latency suggests a memory retention problem. Compare memory trend and SQL duration; a normal query duration helps distinguish memory pressure from slow SQL.

title: Routing latency after deployment
content: Correlate a routing delay regression with deployment timestamps and configuration diffs. A changed retry delay can increase fill latency despite healthy database timings. Request review before rollback.

title: NAV reconciliation mismatch
content: Compare each account using Decimal precision and a one-cent tolerance. An exchange snapshot discrepancy may require settlement investigation. Never overwrite a live ledger from one unverified snapshot.

title: Feature drift with insufficient cause
content: Slippage and heartbeat drift outside a synthetic baseline is an anomaly signal, not a root cause or probability. Obtain additional logs and metrics; abstain if evidence cannot distinguish causes.
